questions.unit: Unit 1: Exploring One-Variable Data and Collecting Data
questions.prompt: Ava completes a cycling course in 36 minutes, where cycling times have mean 42 minutes and standard deviation 4 minutes. Noah completes a rowing course in 438 seconds, where rowing times have mean 480 seconds and standard deviation 30 seconds. Lower times indicate better performance. Who performed farther below the mean of the relevant distribution?

choices.A: Noah, because 42 seconds is a larger raw difference than 6 minutes
choices.B: Ava, because her z-score is −1.50 compared with Noah's z-score of −1.40
choices.C: They performed equally well because both times are below their respective means
choices.D: The performances cannot be compared because the activities use different units

questions.correctAnswerText: Ava, because her z-score is −1.50 compared with Noah's z-score of −1.40
questions.explanation: Ava's standardized time is (36 − 42)/4 = −1.50, and Noah's is (438 − 480)/30 = −1.40. Because lower times are better, Ava performed slightly farther in the favorable direction relative to her distribution.

questions.unit: Unit 2: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
questions.prompt: A random sample of 20 warranty claims is classified as approved or not approved. Which value cannot be the sample proportion p̂ of approved claims?
questions.explanation: With n = 20, p̂ = X/20 for an integer count X, so possible proportions occur in increments of 0.05. The values 0.15, 0.40, and 0.65 correspond to 3, 8, and 13 approvals, but 0.33 does not correspond to an integer count.

questions.unit: Unit 3: Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions
questions.prompt: A county wants to compare the proportions of households that compost food waste in two neighborhoods. Which data-collection plan best supports inference about the difference in household proportions?

choices.A: Independently select a simple random sample of addresses in each neighborhood and record whether each selected household composts.
choices.B: Survey shoppers at a farmers market located between the neighborhoods.
choices.C: Post one online questionnaire and compare respondents who type the two neighborhood names.
choices.D: Survey several people at each selected address and treat every person's response as an independent household.

questions.correctAnswerText: Independently select a simple random sample of addresses in each neighborhood and record whether each selected household composts.
questions.explanation: The household is the observational unit and the response is binary. Independent probability samples from both neighborhoods support inference about the difference in their population proportions.

questions.unit: Unit 4: Inference for Quantitative Data: Means
questions.prompt: A one-sample test of H0: μ = 24 minutes produces t = −2.4. Which interpretation of the test statistic is correct?

choices.A: The sample mean is 2.4 minutes below 24 minutes.
choices.B: The population mean has a 2.4% probability of equaling 24 minutes.
choices.C: The sample mean is 2.4 estimated standard errors below the null mean of 24 minutes.
choices.D: Exactly 2.4% of the observations are below 24 minutes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The sample mean is 2.4 estimated standard errors below the null mean of 24 minutes.
questions.explanation: A t statistic measures the signed distance from the null value in estimated standard-error units. The negative sign indicates x̄ < 24, and the magnitude 2.4 gives the standardized distance, not a raw time or probability.

questions.unit: Unit 5: Regression Analysis
questions.prompt: A regression model predicts equipment temperature y from cooling-airflow setting x. The least-squares slope is −2.4 degrees Celsius per airflow unit. If x increases from 7 to 11, how does the predicted temperature change?

choices.A: It increases by 9.6 degrees Celsius.
choices.B: It decreases by 9.6 degrees Celsius.
choices.C: It decreases by 2.4 degrees Celsius.
choices.D: The change cannot be found without the intercept.

questions.correctAnswerText: It decreases by 9.6 degrees Celsius.
questions.explanation: A slope of −2.4 means each one-unit increase in airflow changes predicted temperature by −2.4 degrees. The four-unit increase gives Δŷ = −2.4(11 − 7) = −9.6 degrees Celsius.

questions.unit: Unit 1: Exploring One-Variable Data and Collecting Data
questions.prompt: A company wants to determine whether a redesigned computer interface reduces data-entry errors. Which plan best supports a causal conclusion for the participating employees?

choices.A: Randomly assign participating employees to the current or redesigned interface, give both groups comparable tasks, and compare error rates.
choices.B: Let employees choose the interface they prefer and compare their error rates.
choices.C: Give the redesigned interface to new employees and the current interface to experienced employees.
choices.D: Ask employees which interface they believe would produce fewer errors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Randomly assign participating employees to the current or redesigned interface, give both groups comparable tasks, and compare error rates.
questions.explanation: Random assignment tends to balance other employee characteristics across the interface groups, and comparable tasks prevent task difficulty from being confounded with interface type.

questions.unit: Unit 3: Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions
questions.prompt: In a test comparing two population proportions under H0: p₁ = p₂, sample 1 has 42 successes among 60 observations and sample 2 has 30 successes among 50 observations. What is the pooled sample proportion?
questions.explanation: Under H0: p₁ = p₂, pool the successes and observations: p̂_pool = (42 + 30)/(60 + 50) = 72/110 ≈ 0.655.

questions.unit: Unit 2: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
questions.prompt: For repeated simple random samples of a fixed size from a population with proportion p, the mean of the sampling distribution of p̂ equals p. What does this property imply?

choices.A: Every random sample produces p̂ = p.
choices.B: Half of all sample proportions are greater than 0.50.
choices.C: The estimator p̂ has no systematic tendency to overestimate or underestimate p, although individual samples vary.
choices.D: The standard deviation of p̂ is zero.

questions.correctAnswerText: The estimator p̂ has no systematic tendency to overestimate or underestimate p, although individual samples vary.
questions.explanation: An estimator whose sampling-distribution mean equals the parameter is unbiased. Unbiasedness is a repeated-sampling property and does not require every estimate to equal p.

questions.unit: Unit 4: Inference for Quantitative Data: Means
questions.prompt: A researcher constructs a 95% one-sample t confidence interval for μ and tests H0: μ = 50 using the same data. If the null value is changed to 52 but the sample data and confidence level are unchanged, which result is guaranteed to remain unchanged?

choices.A: The confidence interval for μ
choices.B: The t statistic
choices.C: The p-value
choices.D: The distance between x̄ and the null value

questions.correctAnswerText: The confidence interval for μ
questions.explanation: A confidence interval is determined by the sample data, confidence level, and procedure; it does not depend on which null value is later tested. Changing the null value changes x̄ − μ0 and therefore generally changes the t statistic and p-value.

questions.unit: Unit 1: Exploring One-Variable Data and Collecting Data
questions.prompt: A transit analyst wants to describe the distribution of delays experienced by buses at a particular intersection. Which choice most clearly identifies appropriate observational units and a quantitative variable?

choices.A: The intersection is the only observational unit, and traffic is labeled light or heavy.
choices.B: Each randomly selected bus passage is an observational unit, and its delay is measured in seconds relative to schedule.
choices.C: Each bus route is a variable, and the drivers are classified by route color.
choices.D: The city's total annual delay is one observational unit measured as delayed or not delayed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each randomly selected bus passage is an observational unit, and its delay is measured in seconds relative to schedule.
questions.explanation: Each bus passage supplies one observation, and delay in seconds is a clearly defined quantitative variable whose distribution can be described.

questions.unit: Unit 5: Regression Analysis
questions.prompt: A laboratory recorded humidity and sensor error together on 30 trials, but someone later sorted the humidity column and error column separately. What is required before a meaningful correlation or regression can be computed?

choices.A: Convert both sorted columns to z-scores and match equal z-scores.
choices.B: Pair the smallest humidity with the largest error to maximize the range.
choices.C: Randomly permute one sorted column and use the resulting pairs.
choices.D: Recover each trial's original humidity-error pairing; if that pairing cannot be recovered, the association cannot be reconstructed from the marginal lists.

questions.correctAnswerText: Recover each trial's original humidity-error pairing; if that pairing cannot be recovered, the association cannot be reconstructed from the marginal lists.
questions.explanation: Correlation and regression depend on which x-value occurred with each y-value. Separately sorted marginal lists preserve individual distributions but destroy the joint pairings that determine association.

questions.unit: Unit 3: Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions
questions.prompt: A 95% confidence interval for a population error proportion p is (0.08, 0.14). A performance standard requires p < 0.10. Which conclusion is justified?

choices.A: The standard is definitely met because the interval contains values below 0.10.
choices.B: The standard is definitely not met because the interval contains values above 0.10.
choices.C: The interval includes plausible values on both sides of 0.10, so it does not establish whether the standard is met.
choices.D: Exactly 10% of the population errors lie between 0.08 and 0.14.

questions.correctAnswerText: The interval includes plausible values on both sides of 0.10, so it does not establish whether the standard is met.
questions.explanation: Because 0.10 lies inside the interval, the data are compatible with a population error proportion both below and above the performance threshold. The interval therefore does not resolve compliance at the stated confidence level.

questions.unit: Unit 2: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
questions.prompt: A binomial random variable X has mean 12 and standard deviation 3. What are the values of n and p?

choices.A: n = 36 and p = 1/3
choices.B: n = 48 and p = 1/4
choices.C: n = 16 and p = 3/4

questions.correctAnswerText: n = 48 and p = 1/4
questions.explanation: For a binomial variable, μ = np = 12 and σ² = np(1 − p) = 9. Thus 1 − p = 9/12 = 3/4, so p = 1/4 and n = 12/(1/4) = 48.

questions.unit: Unit 1: Exploring One-Variable Data and Collecting Data
questions.prompt: An ordered sample contains 9 observations. Its fifth observation, and therefore its median, is 12; its sixth observation is 15. One new value larger than every original observation is added. What is the median of the enlarged sample?
questions.explanation: After a new largest value is added, there are 10 observations. The middle positions are the fifth and sixth original observations, so the new median is (12 + 15)/2 = 13.5.

questions.unit: Unit 4: Inference for Quantitative Data: Means
questions.prompt: Researchers compare two short-term treatments for the same quantitative response using a crossover design. Which feature is most important for limiting treatment-order and carryover effects?

choices.A: Randomize the treatment order for each participant and include an adequate washout period between treatments.
choices.B: Give every participant treatment A first so the procedure is consistent.
choices.C: Let participants select which treatment they receive first.
choices.D: Measure treatment A in the morning and treatment B in the evening for everyone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Randomize the treatment order for each participant and include an adequate washout period between treatments.
questions.explanation: Randomizing order balances systematic order effects, and a washout period reduces carryover from the first treatment into the second treatment period.

questions.unit: Unit 3: Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions
questions.prompt: A company compares the population false-alarm proportions for a new sensor and an old sensor using independent random samples. It seeks evidence that the new sensor has a lower false-alarm proportion. Which hypotheses match the goal?

choices.A: H0: p_new = p_old; Ha: p_new ≠ p_old
choices.B: H0: p_new < p_old; Ha: p_new = p_old
choices.C: H0: p_new = p_old; Ha: p_new < p_old
choices.D: H0: p̂_new = p̂_old; Ha: p̂_new < p̂_old

questions.correctAnswerText: H0: p_new = p_old; Ha: p_new < p_old
questions.explanation: Hypotheses use population parameters, equality belongs in H0, and the claim that the new false-alarm proportion is lower determines a left-tailed alternative.

questions.unit: Unit 2: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
questions.stimulus: The waiting time X, in minutes, for an automated gate has a density curve that is 0 outside 0 ≤ X ≤ 4. From x = 0 to x = 4, the curve is a straight line rising from (0, 0) to (4, 0.5). The total area under the curve is 1.
questions.prompt: The density curve for X is a line from (0, 0) to (4, 0.5). What is P(X ≤ 2)?
questions.explanation: At x = 2, the line's height is 0.25. The probability is the triangular area from 0 to 2: (1/2)(2)(0.25) = 0.250.

questions.unit: Unit 2: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
questions.stimulus: The waiting time X, in minutes, for an automated gate has a density curve that is 0 outside 0 ≤ X ≤ 4. From x = 0 to x = 4, the curve is a straight line rising from (0, 0) to (4, 0.5). The total area under the curve is 1.
questions.prompt: The density curve for X is a line from (0, 0) to (4, 0.5). What is P(X > 3)?
questions.explanation: The triangular area to the left of 3 is (1/2)(3)(0.375) = 9/16. Therefore P(X > 3) = 1 − 9/16 = 7/16.

questions.unit: Unit 2: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
questions.stimulus: The waiting time X, in minutes, for an automated gate has a density curve that is 0 outside 0 ≤ X ≤ 4. From x = 0 to x = 4, the curve is a straight line rising from (0, 0) to (4, 0.5). The total area under the curve is 1.
questions.prompt: The density curve for X is a line from (0, 0) to (4, 0.5). Which value is approximately the median waiting time, with half the area to its left and half to its right?

choices.A: 2.83 minutes
choices.B: 2.00 minutes
choices.C: 3.46 minutes
choices.D: 1.41 minutes

questions.correctAnswerText: 2.83 minutes
questions.explanation: At x = m, the density height is m/8, so the triangular area to the left is (1/2)m(m/8) = m²/16. Setting this area equal to 0.5 gives m = √8 ≈ 2.83 minutes.

questions.unit: Unit 1: Exploring One-Variable Data and Collecting Data
questions.prompt: A distribution of error scores is right-skewed with median 12 and IQR 6. An accuracy score is defined as 100 minus the error score. Which description of the accuracy-score distribution is correct?

choices.A: Right-skewed with median 88 and IQR 94
choices.B: Symmetric with median 100 and IQR 6
choices.C: Left-skewed with median 88 and IQR 6
choices.D: Left-skewed with median −12 and IQR −6

questions.correctAnswerText: Left-skewed with median 88 and IQR 6
questions.explanation: The transformation y = 100 − x reflects the distribution and shifts it, so right skew becomes left skew. The median becomes 100 − 12 = 88, and multiplying by −1 leaves the IQR's magnitude unchanged at 6.

questions.unit: Unit 4: Inference for Quantitative Data: Means
questions.prompt: A researcher duplicates every row of a dataset and then reruns a one-sample t-test. Software reports a smaller standard error and p-value because the displayed sample size doubled. Which assessment is correct?

choices.A: The new result is more precise because every copied row counts as a new independent observation.
choices.B: The apparent gain in precision is invalid because copying observations adds no independent information.
choices.C: The result is valid only if the original sample mean was zero.
choices.D: Duplicating rows changes the population parameter being tested.

questions.correctAnswerText: The apparent gain in precision is invalid because copying observations adds no independent information.
questions.explanation: The copied rows are perfectly dependent duplicates rather than new observations. Treating them as independent artificially inflates n and understates the true standard error.

questions.unit: Unit 3: Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions
questions.prompt: Two independent samples each have size 400. Sample A has p̂_A = 0.10, and sample B has p̂_B = 0.50. Separate 95% confidence intervals are constructed for the two population proportions using the standard one-proportion z-interval. Which interval has the smaller margin of error?

choices.A: Sample A's interval, because 0.10(0.90) is less than 0.50(0.50)
choices.B: Sample B's interval, because 0.50 is farther from 0
choices.C: The margins are equal because the sample sizes and confidence levels are equal
choices.D: The margins cannot be compared without knowing the population sizes

questions.correctAnswerText: Sample A's interval, because 0.10(0.90) is less than 0.50(0.50)
questions.explanation: With the same n and z*, margin of error is proportional to √[p̂(1 − p̂)]. This product is 0.09 for sample A and 0.25 for sample B, so sample A's interval is narrower.

questions.unit: Unit 1: Exploring One-Variable Data and Collecting Data
questions.prompt: An empirical cumulative relative-frequency graph for customer wait times has value 0.72 at 30 seconds. What does this mean?

choices.A: The mean wait time is 30 seconds for 72% of customers.
choices.B: Exactly 28% of wait times equal 30 seconds.
choices.C: The standard deviation of wait times is 0.72 second.
choices.D: Approximately 72% of observed wait times are at most 30 seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approximately 72% of observed wait times are at most 30 seconds.
questions.explanation: An empirical cumulative relative frequency at 30 seconds is the proportion of observations less than or equal to 30 seconds.

questions.unit: Unit 4: Inference for Quantitative Data: Means
questions.prompt: Software output for an unpooled two-sample t procedure reports df = 17.6. A student claims that degrees of freedom must always be an integer. Which assessment is correct?

choices.A: The output is invalid because df must equal the smaller sample size.
choices.B: The output should always use df = n₁ + n₂ − 2.
choices.C: The Welch approximation can produce noninteger df, and software may use 17.6 directly.
choices.D: A noninteger df proves that the observations are paired.

questions.correctAnswerText: The Welch approximation can produce noninteger df, and software may use 17.6 directly.
questions.explanation: The unpooled two-sample t procedure uses an approximate degrees-of-freedom calculation that need not be an integer. Statistical software can evaluate the t distribution at the reported decimal df.

questions.unit: Unit 2: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
questions.prompt: A spinner lands blue with probability 0.20, green with probability 0.30, and gold with probability 0.50. Which assignment of random digits 0 through 9 correctly simulates one spin?

choices.A: 0–1 blue, 2–4 green, 5–9 gold
choices.B: 0–2 blue, 3–5 green, 6–9 gold
choices.C: 0 blue, 1–3 green, 4–9 gold
choices.D: 0–1 blue, 2–5 green, 6–9 gold

questions.correctAnswerText: 0–1 blue, 2–4 green, 5–9 gold
questions.explanation: The assignment gives 2 of 10 digits to blue, 3 of 10 to green, and 5 of 10 to gold, matching probabilities 0.20, 0.30, and 0.50.

questions.unit: Unit 1: Exploring One-Variable Data and Collecting Data
questions.prompt: A probability sample for a mailed public-library survey has a low response rate. Which follow-up plan is most useful for assessing possible nonresponse bias?

choices.A: Replace every nonrespondent with the nearest person listed in the directory.
choices.B: Increase the reported sample size by counting each respondent twice.
choices.C: Compare early respondents with later respondents only and assume they represent all nonrespondents.
choices.D: Randomly select a subset of nonrespondents for intensive follow-up and compare their answers with those of initial respondents.

questions.correctAnswerText: Randomly select a subset of nonrespondents for intensive follow-up and compare their answers with those of initial respondents.
questions.explanation: Intensive follow-up can reveal whether people who initially failed to respond differ systematically from respondents. Convenience replacement or double-counting cannot diagnose the bias.

questions.unit: Unit 3: Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions
questions.prompt: Under a null hypothesis of no treatment effect, 5,000 random reassignments are generated. In 73 reassignments, the absolute difference in sample proportions is at least as large as the observed absolute difference. What is the randomization-test p-value?
questions.explanation: The simulation already counts results at least as extreme in either direction by using the absolute difference. Therefore the estimated p-value is 73/5,000 = 0.0146, with no additional doubling.

questions.unit: Unit 5: Regression Analysis
questions.prompt: Two laboratory instruments measure the same concentration. Their readings have correlation r = 0.98, but the new instrument consistently reads about 5 units higher than the old instrument. Which conclusion is most appropriate?

choices.A: The instruments agree closely because a correlation near 1 guarantees equal readings.
choices.B: The new instrument is more precise because its readings are larger.
choices.C: The readings have a strong linear association, but high correlation does not rule out systematic disagreement.
choices.D: Subtracting 5 from the new readings would make the correlation equal to 0.

questions.correctAnswerText: The readings have a strong linear association, but high correlation does not rule out systematic disagreement.
questions.explanation: Correlation measures the strength of linear association, not equality or agreement. Adding a constant to one instrument's readings can preserve r while producing a systematic offset.

questions.unit: Unit 4: Inference for Quantitative Data: Means
questions.prompt: For two independent populations, an estimate of μ₁ − μ₂ is 2.0 units with standard error 1.0 unit. What is the t statistic for testing H0: μ₁ − μ₂ = 5.0?
questions.explanation: The statistic compares the estimated difference with the null difference: t = [2.0 − 5.0]/1.0 = −3.0.

questions.unit: Unit 1: Exploring One-Variable Data and Collecting Data
questions.prompt: A normal distribution has standard deviation 8. The z-scores of its first and third quartiles are approximately −0.674 and 0.674. What is the IQR of the distribution?

choices.A: Approximately 10.8
choices.B: Approximately 5.4
choices.C: Approximately 8.0
choices.D: Approximately 16.0

questions.correctAnswerText: Approximately 10.8
questions.explanation: The IQR is the distance from Q1 to Q3: [0.674 − (−0.674)](8) = 1.348(8) = 10.784, approximately 10.8.

questions.unit: Unit 2: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
questions.prompt: A bike-share agency wants to estimate the probability distribution of the daily number of rentals over an entire year. Which data-collection plan is most appropriate?

choices.A: Record only the ten days with the largest numbers of rentals.
choices.B: Use every day in July because summer has the greatest activity.
choices.C: Select dates at random from throughout the full year and record the number of rentals on each selected date.
choices.D: Ask riders to report how many rentals they believe occur on a typical day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Select dates at random from throughout the full year and record the number of rentals on each selected date.
questions.explanation: Random selection across the entire year represents seasonal and weekday variation in the target distribution. Selecting only busy or summer days would bias the distribution upward.

questions.unit: Unit 3: Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions
questions.prompt: For a right-tailed one-proportion z-test of H0: p = 0.50 with n = 100, reject H0 when z > 1.645. What is the smallest number of successes that will lead to rejection?
questions.explanation: Under H0, SE₀ = √[0.50(0.50)/100] = 0.05. Rejection requires (p̂ − 0.50)/0.05 > 1.645, so p̂ > 0.58225. The smallest attainable proportion above that cutoff is 59/100, corresponding to 59 successes.

questions.unit: Unit 1: Exploring One-Variable Data and Collecting Data
questions.prompt: A food scientist studies the effects of oven temperature (low or high) and convection fan setting (off or on) on crust crispness. Which design best permits separate assessment of both factors and their combination?

choices.A: Randomly assign similar loaves to all four temperature-by-fan treatment combinations, with replication in each combination.
choices.B: Use low temperature only when the fan is off and high temperature only when the fan is on.
choices.C: Let bakers choose one of the four combinations for each loaf.
choices.D: Apply the four combinations on four different days with no random assignment or replication.

questions.correctAnswerText: Randomly assign similar loaves to all four temperature-by-fan treatment combinations, with replication in each combination.
questions.explanation: A replicated factorial design varies both factors in all combinations. Random assignment permits fair comparisons of temperature, fan setting, and how their effects may work together.

questions.unit: Unit 5: Regression Analysis
questions.stimulus:
Three calibration trials produced the paired data below. A least-squares line predicts response y from intensity setting x.

x: 1  2  3
y: 2  4  3
questions.prompt: For the paired data (1, 2), (2, 4), and (3, 3), what is the least-squares regression line predicting y from x?

choices.C: ŷ = 1 + x

questions.explanation: Here x̄ = 2 and ȳ = 3. The slope is Σ[(x − 2)(y − 3)]/Σ(x − 2)² = 1/2 = 0.5, and the intercept is 3 − 0.5(2) = 2.

questions.unit: Unit 5: Regression Analysis
questions.stimulus:
Three calibration trials produced the paired data below. A least-squares line predicts response y from intensity setting x.

x: 1  2  3
y: 2  4  3
questions.prompt: For the paired data (1, 2), (2, 4), and (3, 3), the least-squares line is ŷ = 2 + 0.5x. What is the residual for the trial with x = 3?
questions.explanation: At x = 3, ŷ = 2 + 0.5(3) = 3.5. The residual is observed minus predicted, 3 − 3.5 = −0.5.

questions.unit: Unit 5: Regression Analysis
questions.stimulus:
Three calibration trials produced the paired data below. A least-squares line predicts response y from intensity setting x.

x: 1  2  3
y: 2  4  3
questions.prompt: For the paired data (1, 2), (2, 4), and (3, 3), the least-squares line is ŷ = 2 + 0.5x. Which trial is fitted least closely in the vertical direction?

choices.A: The trial with x = 1, because its residual is −0.5
choices.B: The trial with x = 2, because its residual is 1 and has the largest absolute value
choices.C: The trial with x = 3, because the intensity setting is largest
choices.D: All three trials are fitted equally closely because they determine the line

questions.correctAnswerText: The trial with x = 2, because its residual is 1 and has the largest absolute value
questions.explanation: The residuals for x = 1, 2, and 3 are −0.5, 1, and −0.5. The x = 2 trial has the greatest vertical distance from the line and the largest squared residual contribution.

questions.unit: Unit 4: Inference for Quantitative Data: Means
questions.prompt: Participants are randomly assigned to rehabilitation program A or B, and each participant is measured before and after the program. Researchers want to compare the population mean changes for the two programs. Which analysis matches the goal?

choices.A: A one-proportion z-test using the number who improve
choices.B: A paired t-test pairing one participant from program A with one from program B
choices.C: Compute each participant's after-minus-before change, then use a two-sample t procedure to compare mean changes between programs.
choices.D: A one-sample t procedure using all before measurements only

questions.correctAnswerText: Compute each participant's after-minus-before change, then use a two-sample t procedure to compare mean changes between programs.
questions.explanation: Each participant supplies one change score, preserving the within-person before/after pairing. The program A and B groups are independent, so their mean change scores are compared with a two-sample t procedure.

questions.unit: Unit 2: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
questions.prompt: A random voucher credit X can equal 0, 10, or 20 dollars. Its probabilities are P(X = 0) = 0.50, P(X = 10) = q, and P(X = 20) = 0.50 − q. If E(X) = 6 dollars, what are q and P(X = 20)?
questions.explanation: The mean condition gives 10q + 20(0.50 − q) = 6. Thus 10 − 10q = 6, so q = 0.40 and P(X = 20) = 0.50 − 0.40 = 0.10.

questions.unit: Unit 3: Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions
questions.prompt: In a sample of n = 200, p̂ = 0.30. For a confidence interval, the estimated standard error uses p̂. For testing H0: p = 0.20, the null standard error uses p0 = 0.20. Which pair of standard errors is correct?

choices.A: 0.0283 for the interval and 0.0324 for the test
choices.B: 0.0300 for both procedures
choices.C: 0.0324 for both procedures
choices.D: 0.0324 for the interval and 0.0283 for the test

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.0324 for the interval and 0.0283 for the test

questions.unit: Unit 3: Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions
questions.prompt: A right-tailed test of H0: p = 0.50 is designed to have power 0.80 when p = 0.60. With the same sample size and significance level, what should generally happen to power if the true proportion is p = 0.70?

choices.A: It should fall below 0.50 because 0.70 is farther from the null value.
choices.B: It should be greater than 0.80 because 0.70 is farther into the direction specified by Ha.
choices.C: It must remain exactly 0.80 for every value in Ha.
choices.D: It becomes the significance level because H0 is false.

questions.correctAnswerText: It should be greater than 0.80 because 0.70 is farther into the direction specified by Ha.
questions.explanation: With n and α fixed, values farther from the null in the alternative direction are more likely to fall in the rejection region, so power increases.

questions.unit: Unit 1: Exploring One-Variable Data and Collecting Data
questions.prompt: A city wants to estimate how the proportion of commuters using bicycles changes between this year and four years from now. Which plan best supports comparison of the city populations at the two times?

choices.A: Take an independent probability sample of city commuters at each time using comparable questions and sampling frames.
choices.B: Survey only current bicycle commuters and contact the same volunteers four years later.
choices.C: Compare responses from two open social-media polls conducted four years apart.
choices.D: Ask current commuters to predict how they will travel four years from now.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take an independent probability sample of city commuters at each time using comparable questions and sampling frames.
questions.explanation: Comparable probability samples at both times represent the changing commuter populations. Tracking only current bicycle commuters or using voluntary polls would not estimate the two citywide proportions fairly.

questions.unit: Unit 1: Exploring One-Variable Data and Collecting Data
questions.prompt: Two samples have the same size. The median of sample A is 10, and the median of sample B is 20. What can be concluded about the median of the combined sample?

choices.A: It must be 10.
choices.B: It must be 15.
choices.C: It cannot be determined from the two sample medians alone.
choices.D: It must be 20.

questions.correctAnswerText: It cannot be determined from the two sample medians alone.
questions.explanation: The combined middle positions depend on how all observations from the two samples interleave. Equal sample sizes and the two separate medians do not determine those positions.
